6 inches, or a water depth in conformance with the manufacturer's installation instructions, for a swimming pool slide designed to slow an individual to a near stop at the end of the slide;
A cushioned landing mat below the end of a swimming pool slide if there is a potential for impact or abrasion injury;

A centerline distance from the end of a slide to a wall, lifeline, transition point, centerline from another slide, or obstruction that eliminates the potential for an individual using the slide to strike a wall, lifeline, transition point, an individual using another slide, or an obstruction;
A minimum side distance of 4 feet from the centerline of a slide to a wall, lifeline, transition point, or obstruction;
A design that eliminates the potential for an individual to strike the pool deck or coping while traveling down the swimming pool slide;
A slide end that extends beyond the pool wall, deck, and coping; and
A minimum side distance of 12 feet between the centerline of a slide and a diving board, diving platform, or starting block.
Water Slides.
An owner shall ensure that a water slide:
Complies with the conditions set forth in COMAR 09.12.63 as evidenced by written documentation in accordance with §C(2) of this regulation; and
Exits to a plunge pool or slide runout.
The written documentation of compliance with COMAR 09.12.63 shall be provided by either:
The Maryland Department of Labor; or

If the water slide is not subject to regulation by the Maryland Department of Labor, a registered professional engineer who certifies that the water slide meets the design criteria set forth in COMAR 09.12.63.07.
Wave Pools. An owner shall ensure that a wave pool is provided with an emergency shut-off switch at each guard station.
Tube Rides. An owner shall ensure that a tube ride has designated entry and exit points.
Spray Pools. An owner shall ensure that a spray pool has:
A bottom that slopes from 1/4 inch per foot to 5/8 inch per foot to a drain with grate;
No standing water; and
No obstruction less than 4 feet in height.
Single-Lane Lap Pools. An owner shall ensure that a single-lane pool used for swimming laps has:
A minimum width of 7 1/2 feet; and
A sign on the deck that reads, "Warning: No Diving—Shallow Water" if the water depth is 5 feet or less.
Decorative Fountains and Waterfalls. An owner shall ensure that a decorative fountain or waterfall installed in or connected to a pool or spa does not create a health or safety hazard.
Additional Fixtures. An owner shall ensure that any spray fixture, fountain, piece of play equipment, bridge, ramp, stair, float, swing, or other recreational equipment located within a pool or spa:
Is designed to eliminate or minimize safety hazards such as entrapment, concealment, slipping, abrasions, cuts, punctures, falls, trip hazards, impact injury, and drowning;
Is limited to a shallow water area;
Has a color that contrasts with the pool or spa so that the structure is highly visible;
Has pipes or support columns that are at least 6 inches in diameter;
Is provided with an overhead clearance of at least 7 feet from the pool floor and 4 feet from the water surface where a person may walk under the fixture;
Is provided with recirculated, treated pool water for a spray, stream, or other flow of water; and
Is installed according to the manufacturer's directions.
Filtration Requirements. An owner shall ensure that:
At least two interconnected main drains are installed in the deepest part of a pool and are connected to the filtration system;
A pump reservoir or surge tank is provided for a slide or water feature circulation pump intake, and the pump reservoir or surge tank:
Is made of concrete or other impervious material with a smooth slip-resistant finish;
Has inlets through a weir or a gravity-fed drain with a secure grate;
Has a volume equal to 2 minutes of the combined flow of all pumps connected to the reservoir or tank;
Is accessible only to authorized individuals;
Has pump intakes located in the pump reservoir that are designed to allow cleaning without danger of entrapment; and
The water velocity through grate or drain openings does not exceed 2 feet per second;
A slide or water feature circulation pump has a check valve on the discharge side; and
Returns from a filtration system are placed to provide even and positive circulation and to eliminate any dead spots.

section.heading: Standards for Legacy Public Wading Pools.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy public wading pool is in compliance with:

para.text: This chapter;
Applicable State and local laws, regulations, and ordinances; and
The American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools.

section.heading: Standards for Legacy Public Therapy Pools.

para.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy public therapy pool is in compliance with:
This chapter;
Applicable State and local laws, regulations, and ordinances; and
The American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools.
Minimum Requirements.
An owner shall ensure that a legacy public therapy pool has:

A deck with a minimum width of 4 feet around at least 50 percent of the therapy pool that provides access to individuals using the therapy pool, not including any ramp, entrance area, or exercise area; and
A transition area between a shallow and a deep area that meets one of the conditions in §B(2) of this regulation.
The transition area of a legacy public therapy pool shall have either:
A floor slope that does not exceed 1 foot of drop to 3 feet of run; or
Steps or ramps with handrails or a swing lift to transfer bathers from a shallow area to a deep area.
A legacy public therapy pool shall only be used only for the purpose of supervised therapy.

section.heading: Legacy User Load.
section.text: The Secretary shall determine the user load for a legacy pool or spa, based on the following criteria:

para.text: For a legacy pool and its deck, one individual is allowed for:
Every 12 square feet of water surface in shallow areas;
Every 15 square feet of water surface in areas exceeding 5 feet of water depth, excluding a diving area; and
The 300 square-foot diving area required for each diving board or diving platform;
For a legacy spa, one individual is allowed for every 9 square feet of water surface; and
For a legacy therapy pool, one individual is allowed for every:
Therapy station; or
20 square feet of water surface, whichever is less.

section.heading: Legacy Public Pool or Spa Site.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy public pool or spa site:

para.text: Drains away from the pool or spa area;
Has water and waste water facilities that conform to the requirements of:
Local plumbing code requirements;
Has a walkway between a pool or spa and appurtenant buildings such as a bathhouse or equipment room; and
Complies with applicable State and local laws, regulations, and ordinances.

Except as set forth in §§B—D of this regulation, an owner of a legacy pool or spa shall ensure that a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa, including the required deck area, is completely surrounded by a barrier that complies with the following requirements:
The top of the barrier is at least 72 inches above grade measured on the side of the barrier that faces away from the pool or spa;
The maximum vertical clearance between grade and the bottom of the barrier is 4 inches measured on the side of the barrier that faces away from the pool or spa;

Except when a door or gate that allows access to the pool or spa area enclosed by the barrier is open, an opening in the barrier including in a door or gate does not allow passage of a sphere 4 inches in diameter;
Fence pickets have a maximum separation of 4 inches;

The barrier discourages climbing by preventing access to nearby structures to facilitate climbing, such as light poles, site furnishings, overhanging tree limbs, or other obvious footholds or handholds;
A barrier with horizontal members less than 45 inches apart measured top to top does not have:
Vertical openings greater than 1-3/4 inches in width; or
Horizontal members on the outside of the barrier;
The barrier does not have decorative cutouts greater than 1-3/4 inches in width;
A chain link fence has a maximum mesh size of 2-1/4 inches;
A lattice fence has a maximum mesh size of 1-3/4 inches;
Except as provided in §A(11) and (12) of this regulation, a door or gate that allows access to the pool or spa area enclosed by the barrier shall:
Have the release to open the door or gate located:
At least 54 inches from the floor level; or
Between 34 and 48 inches from the floor level when an electronic or combination mechanical release device is used to release the door or gate;
Open away from the pool or spa area;
Have an opening that provides a minimum width of 32 inches between the gate or door stop and the face of the gate or door with the gate or door open 90 degrees; and
Comply with Regulation .46 of this chapter;
A door or gate that allows access to the pool or spa area enclosed by the barrier and is designated as fire egress from a building:
May not be included in any facility approved for construction after May 27, 2022; and
Is exempt from §A(10)(b) of this regulation;
A door or gate used exclusively for maintenance or service access is exempt from §A(10)(a)—(d) of this regulation; and
A window that is a part of the barrier may not be able to be opened more than 4 inches.
An owner shall ensure that a barrier at a legacy semipublic pool or semipublic spa:
Has a minimum height of 60 inches; and
Has a gate that is self-closing and self-latching.

Except as provided in §D of this regulation, an owner may surround a legacy pool and spa, multiple pools, or multiple spas at one facility with one barrier instead of separate barriers for each pool or spa.
An owner shall ensure that a wading pool or infant pool is separated from a legacy pool or spa by a barrier that has:
A minimum height of 36 inches;
A maximum 4-inch separation between the deck and the bottom of the barrier;
No opening that allows the passage of a sphere 4 inches in diameter; and
An entrance gate with a latch.
An owner shall ensure that:
A deck at a legacy recreational or semipublic pool:
Completely surrounds the pool;
Is continuous with a minimum unobstructed width of 4 feet and an average width of 6 feet, and
Is in conformance with the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools;
A deck at a public spa is in conformance with the American National Standard for Public Spas;
The slope of a deck is away from a pool or a spa, toward points of disposal, and not less than 1/4 inch per foot, or greater than 1/2 inch per foot;
The deck has drainage to deck drains or other points of disposal;
A brick, stone, aggregate, or similar deck surface has a subdeck in the required deck area; and
A wood deck has a gravel and plastic ground barrier or a concrete subdeck in the required deck area.
An owner of a legacy pool or spa may:
Include the pool or spa coping in the measurement of the deck width; and
Have ladders, handrails, lifeguard stands, structures for use by disabled individuals, and other pool equipment on the deck.

Except as provided in §B(2) of this regulation, an owner may not have light poles, structural supports, decorative fountains, waterfalls, and other obstacles or obstructions within 4 feet of a pool or within the required deck area of a spa.

section.heading: Legacy Equipment Rooms.
section.text: An owner of a legacy pool or spa shall ensure that a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has an equipment room that:

para.text: Houses the pool or spa circulation, filtration, and disinfection equipment;
Has:
Weathertight construction to prevent the entrance of precipitation;
Adequate floor area for safe access to all equipment;
A minimum ceiling height of 7 feet 6 inches;
A waterproof floor that drains to a floor drain;
A lockable entrance door that allows complete and unencumbered access to the equipment room;
A minimum of 20 footcandles of artificial illumination;

Ventilation sized at 2 cubic feet per minute per square foot of floor area that is either mechanical exhaust ventilation if chemicals are used or stored in the equipment room, or natural or mechanical exhaust ventilation if chemicals are not used or stored in the equipment room;
Adequate make-up air to replace the air exhausted by the ventilation system; and
A hose bibb with an atmospheric vacuum breaker; and
Allows easy access to valves, controls, gauges, filters, pumps, feeders, and other operating equipment.

section.heading: Legacy Pipe Material.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that pipe material for a legacy public pool or spa conforms to COMAR 09.20.01.

para.text: Gauges and Release Valves. An owner of a legacy pool or spa shall ensure that the circulation system for a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa includes the following:
A pressure gauge on the filter or on the influent side of the filter piping;
A pressure gauge on the effluent side of the filter piping;
A vacuum or compound gauge on the influent side of a pump;
A flow meter that:
Indicates the rate of flow through the circulation system;
Has a permanent scale readable in gallons per minute;
Is accurate to within 10 percent of the actual flow; and
Reads in the range encompassing the minimum and maximum flow rate;
A thermometer on the return line to a pool or spa if the circulation system includes a heating system; and
A manually operated air release valve on a pressure filter or a separation tank, or both.
Turnover Rate.
An owner of a legacy pool or spa shall ensure that a recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa is maintained to produce the following minimum turnover rates, with continuous 24-hour flow:
Pools for swimming and diving: Minimum turnover rate = volume of pool in gallons/480 minutes;
Pools for water recreational attractions and therapy: Minimum turnover rate = volume of pool in gallons/360 minutes;
Pools for wading have a minimum turnover rate equal to the greater of:
Volume of pool in gallons/120 minutes; or
The minimum flow required for the skimmer system and main drain to operate according to the manufacturer's specifications; or
Spas: Minimum turnover rate = volume of spa/30 minutes.
An owner of a legacy pool or spa shall ensure that a limited public-use pool has a turnover rate in conformance with:
The American National Standard for Residential Inground Swimming Pools; or
The American National Standard for Aboveground/Onground Residential Swimming Pools.
Head Loss Calculations. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that head loss calculations include the following:
Piping head loss, found by using:
The Hazen-Williams formula which is: piping head loss per 100 feet of pipe = 0.2083 (100 / C)1.852(Q1.852/ D4.865)
where:
D = nominal inside diameter of pipe;
Q = gpm; and
C = constant for inside roughness of pipe; or
Standard engineering tables;

Equipment head loss, including filters, valves, heaters, and other circulation equipment, based on the manufacturers' specifications for the equipment at the design flow rate, and filter pressure differential with the filter in a clean and in a dirty condition;
Elevation of pump suction and discharge in relation to the pool or spa water surface level; and
Determination of the total dynamic head of the circulation system for use in pump selection.
Surface to Bottom Flow Ratio.
An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that:
Piping for surface outlets is designed to accommodate 80 percent of the flow; and
Piping for bottom outlets is designed to accommodate 20 percent of the flow.
An owner of a recreational pool or semipublic pool may have a gutter surface overflow system with a flow design of 50 percent from the surface outlets and 50 percent from the bottom outlets.

Filter Capacity. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that a filter has a filtration capacity sufficient to operate in the range between the minimum turnover rate and the filter design flow rate when the circulation system is at the:
Lowest level of calculated total dynamic head when the filter is in a clean condition; and
Highest level of calculated total dynamic head when the filter pressure differential is at the maximum allowed in Regulation .23I(5) of this chapter.
Interconnections Between Pools. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that a pool is not interconnected with a:
Spa or wading pool except during the filling of a spa or wading pool; and
Spray pool.

Except as provided in §B of this regulation, an owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that circulation system components, including skimmers, pumps, filters, multiport valves, adjustable output rate chemical feeders, flow-through chemical feeders, chemical process equipment, chlorine generators, ion generators, and other pool and spa equipment comply with Circulation System Components and Related Materials for Pools, Spas/Hot Tubs.

The Secretary shall accept legacy swimming pool, spa, or hot tub circulation system components as meeting the requirements set forth in §A of this regulation if these items are in the current published NSF listing of swimming pool, spa, or hot tub circulation system components or a listing from organizations accredited by the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) for the certification of circulation system components.
Chemical Feeder and Process Equipment. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that the capacity of chemical feeder and process equipment is adequate to:
Provide the minimum required disinfectant residual to the pool or spa water, as required in Regulation .16A of this chapter; and
Establish a breakpoint when the combined chlorine level is over 0.2 ppm.
Chlorine Gas Feeders. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that the:
Equipment installation, and operation of a chlorine gas feeder are in compliance with the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools:
Except that the word "shall" is substituted for the word "should"; and
Which shall comply with the specifications of Appendix E; and
Recirculated water is treated downstream of the chlorine gas injection point to maintain the water's pH between 7.2 and 7.8.
Vacuum Systems.
An owner shall ensure that a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has a vacuum system for cleaning the pool or spa floor.
An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa may use skimmer outlet pipes for vacuum purposes for circulation systems with four or fewer skimmers.

For circulation systems with more than four skimmers or a gutter system, an owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that a vacuum system is provided that is separate from the skimmer or gutter system.
If vacuum fittings are provided within a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa, the owner shall ensure that the fittings are:
Located at convenient locations approximately 1 foot below the water surface; and
Provided with flush removable caps.

When the vacuum system is an integral part of the circulation system, an owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that the vacuum line connection is before the pump hair and lint strainer.
Carbon Dioxide Feeders. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that a carbon dioxide feeder system is:
Installed and maintained in accordance with the manufacturer's specifications;
Located in a ventilated area; and
Secured to prevent damage to the gas cylinder if the cylinder is subject to tipping.
Ozone Systems. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that:
An ultraviolet light ozone system is used and installed according to Circulation System Components and Related Materials for Pools, Spas/Hot Tubs;
A corona discharge ozone system is used and installed according to Circulation System Components and Related Materials for Pools, Spas/Hot Tubs, and the following requirements:
The system is designed to provide a minimum concentration of ozone generated to be 1.5 percent by weight;
The ozone gas is diffused through a static mixer into a contact column with a sidestream flow of recirculated water equal to a minimum of 5 percent of the required turnover rate;
The system is designed to provide a contact time of 2 minutes when used in conjunction with a chlorine disinfectant, or 1 minute when used in conjunction with a bromine disinfectant;

The system provides a minimum contact time value of 0.5 milligram/liter in the contact column when the contact time value equals the concentration of dissolved ozone in milligrams/liter times the contact time in minutes;
The air feed, which is natural or oxygen enriched air, is filtered to remove particulates and dehumidified to a minimum dew point of minus 60°C before the ozone generating chamber;
An ozone gas feed line is ozone resistant;
Valves are provided to control flow through the system;
Offgas venting from the contact column is:
Equipped with an ozone destruct system that removes all ozone before release to the atmosphere; or
Returned to the main recirculation line when used in conjunction with a bromine disinfectant;
When necessary, a foam suppression system is provided before offgas venting;
The oxidation reduction potential of the sidestream after contact and before dissolved ozone removal is a minimum of 650 millivolts;
The dissolved ozone is removed from the sidestream using granulated activated carbon before remixing with the recirculated water when used in conjunction with a chlorine disinfectant;
The ozone generating system shuts off if the water recirculating system shuts off or if the vacuum is lost on the ozone gas output line;
The ozone gas output is under negative pressure or a vacuum;
The ozone generation area is ventilated at 2 cfm per square foot of floor area to prevent the build up of excess ozone; and
The recirculated water is treated to maintain the pH between 7.2 and 7.8.

An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa may connect an equalization line for a skimmer to the main drain line in a wading pool, or other pool that does not have sufficient water depth, for the installation of the equalizer line through the pool wall below the skimmer throat.

Competitive Aquatic Events. An owner of a legacy public pool used for accredited competitive aquatic events as defined in §3 of the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools shall ensure compliance with §6.4.1 of the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools.

Diving Equipment. An owner of a legacy public pool shall ensure that diving equipment is installed in compliance with §§7.2.5—7.2.5.6 of the American National Standards for Public Swimming Pools.
Diving Board Clearance. An owner of a legacy public pool shall ensure that unobstructed clearance is provided for a diving board in conformance with the following minimum dimensions:
A minimum height of 13 feet measured upward from the plummet of a diving board or greater than 13 feet if specified by the manufacturer of the diving board;
A clearance as required in §D(1) of this regulation extending:
16 feet forward of the plummet;
8 feet behind the plummet; and
8 feet to both sides of the plummet;
A minimum distance of 10 feet between the plummets of adjacent diving boards; and
A minimum distance between a diving board plummet and a side wall of:
10 feet for a diving board 20 inches or less above the water line; and
12 feet for a diving board greater than 20 inches above the water line.

Diving Boards Over Ten Feet Above Water. An owner of a legacy public pool shall ensure that diving boards in excess of 10 feet above the water line and diving platforms are in compliance with §7.2.4 of the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools.
Starting Blocks. An owner of a legacy public pool shall ensure that a starting block:
Is located on the pool deck so that a swimmer dives into a minimum of 5 feet water depth; or
At a pool constructed before February 10, 1997, is located so that a swimmer dives into a minimum of:
5 feet water depth when the starting block is used without supervision; or
4 feet water depth when the starting block is:
Used in a controlled environment such as a swimming competition under the supervision of an instructor; and​
Restricted from unsupervised use or is removed when not under supervised use.
To prevent a suction entrapment hazard, an owner of a legacy public pool or spa shall ensure that the requirements of §B—D are met.

Main Drain. The owner of a legacy public pool or spa shall ensure that a main drain, drain covering, outlet, fitting, and maximum velocity complies with 15 U.S.C. §8003 and ANSI/PHTA/ICC-7 2020, as incorporated by reference in Regulation .03 of this chapter.

Outlets, Fittings, and Maximum Velocity. The owner of a legacy pool or spa shall ensure the maximum velocity in the design of the drain piping does not exceed 6 feet per second when 100 percent of the circulation system design flow is drawn through the drain piping of any single drain.
Skimmers. The owner of a legacy public pool or spa shall ensure that a skimmer is:
Connected to an equalization line, main drain line, vent, or another skimmer that cannot be isolated by a valve or other means; or
Provided with a vented lid.

section.heading: Legacy Chemical Storage Area.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has a chemical storage area that has:

para.text: A lockable door which can be opened from the inside; and
Ventilation that is sized at 2 cfm per square foot of floor area and that exhausts to the open air.

section.heading: Legacy Hydrostatic Relief Valves.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy inground recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has hydrostatic relief valves as needed to relieve the hydrostatic pressure from ground water when the pool or spa is empty.

section.heading: Legacy Ventilation of Indoor Facilities.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy indoor recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has:

para.text: A ventilating system capable of exhausting 1 1/2 cfm of air per square foot of enclosed area or dehumidifying the recirculated air from the enclosed area; and
Make-up air equal to the volume of exhausted air or as required in the specifications for the ventilation system.
Water Supply System. An owner shall ensure that a water supply system at a legacy public pool or spa is in conformance with:
COMAR 09.20.01; and
Local plumbing code requirements.
Sewage Disposal System. An owner shall ensure that a sewage disposal system at a legacy public pool or spa is in conformance with:
COMAR 09.20.01; and
Local plumbing code requirements.

Drinking Fountains. An owner shall ensure that a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa enclosure has at least one drinking fountain for every 5,000 square feet of water surface area.
Hose Bibbs. An owner of a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa shall ensure that the following locations have an accessible hose bibb equipped with an atmospheric vacuum breaker:
On the deck at 150 feet intervals;
In an equipment room; and
In both a men's and a women's bathhouse.
Fill Spouts. If a fill spout is installed at a legacy public pool or spa, the owner shall ensure that the fill spout is:

Installed within 10 inches of a ladder or handrail or in front of a lifeguard stand whose supports are immediately adjacent to the pool or spa rim, so that the fill spout does not present a tripping hazard or a puncture hazard;
Not installed over a seat bench;
Braced or constructed so the fill spout does not flex downward; and
Provided with a flexible cover on the tip of the fill spout if the spout presents a potential for injury to an individual using a pool or spa.
Backflow Prevention. An owner of a legacy public pool or spa shall ensure that:
A pool or spa facility has backflow protection for:
A potable water supply, in accordance with COMAR 09.20.01; and
Wastewater, in accordance with COMAR 09.20.01; and
An air gap that is two times the diameter of the fill spout separates the fill spout from the flood rim level of the pool or spa.

section.heading: Legacy Toilet, Hand Sink, and Shower Facilities.

para.text: Except as provided in §B of this regulation, an owner shall ensure that a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa has:

A bathhouse, toilets, hand sinks, and showers within 100 feet of an entrance gate to the pool or spa in accordance with the American National Standard for Public Swimming Pools, Articles 19.1—19.6.13;
At least a minimum number of toilets, hand sinks, and showers based on:
The maximum user load of the pool or spa set forth in Regulation .32 of this chapter;
Fixture ratios set forth in §A(1) of this regulation; and
State and local building codes;
50 percent of the required fixtures designated for use by each sex, unless the pool or spa is for one sex only; and
At least 50 percent of the required showers are located within a bathhouse.
An owner is not required to provide toilet, hand sink, and shower facilities at a legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa when bathers have access to equivalent facilities in:
Living quarters not more than 500 feet from a pool or a spa entrance; or
A building or buildings not more than 500 feet from a pool or a spa entrance.

An owner shall ensure that equivalent facilities used by legacy recreational pool, semipublic pool, or public spa bathers and patrons of a recreational center, health club, marina, or other facility are in compliance with:
§A of this regulation; and
State or local plumbing codes regarding fixtures and dressing area for the patrons sharing the equivalent facilities.

section.heading: Accommodations for Disabled Individuals.
section.text: An owner shall ensure that a legacy public pool or spa is in compliance with all applicable federal, State, and local codes governing facilities for disabled individuals, including COMAR 05.02.02.

para.text: The application for an identification card for a minor under 15 years old shall be cosigned by a parent or a legal guardian of the applicant. If the applicant has no parent or legal guardian, an adult employer of the applicant or any other responsible adult over 18 years old can cosign.
The individual cosigning the application of a minor shall certify that the statements made in the application are true to the best of the cosigner's knowledge, information, and belief.

section.heading: Duplicate.
section.text: A duplicate identification card may be issued to replace one which has been lost, stolen, mutilated, or destroyed if the person applying for a duplicate card furnishes information satisfactory to the Administration of the above circumstances, pays the required fee, and is entitled to a duplicate identification card.

para.text: Upon receipt from the identification cardholder, on a change request form prescribed by the Administration, the Administration shall issue an attachment card to correct the resident address.
There is no fee for the attachment card.

Upon request by the identification cardholder, on a form prescribed by the Administration, the Administration shall issue a new identification card instead of the attachment card. The applicant shall appear in person and pay a fee as set forth in COMAR 11.11.05.
There is no fee for adding or deleting:
An organ donor designation to an identification card;
A veteran designation to an identification card;
A nonapparent disability designation to an identification card; or
A blind or visual impairment designation to an identification card.

section.heading: Fees Not Refundable.
section.text: The fees authorized by Transportation Article, §12-301, Annotated Code of Maryland, and this chapter for issuance, duplication, correction, or renewal of the identification cards may not be refunded.

para.text: For purposes of this regulation, the word “blind” means:
Visual acuity not to exceed 20/200 in the better eye with correcting lenses; or
Visual acuity greater than 20/200 but with a limitation in the fields of vision such that the widest diameter of the visual field subtends an angle not greater than 20 degrees.
A fee is not required if the applicant for an identification card is exempt under Transportation Article, §12-301(b)(2), Annotated Code of Maryland.
An application for a waiver of fees pursuant to Transportation Article, §12-301(b)(2)(ii)—(iv), Annotated Code of Maryland, may be required to be accompanied by a:
Card issued by a governmental agency or tax exempt organization attesting to the disability; or
Signed statement by a licensed physician attesting to the permanent disability, except in a case when a loss of limb is clearly visible.

section.heading: Grounds for Disciplinary Action or Denial.

para.text: The State Superintendent of Schools shall suspend, deny, or revoke a license and all specific license areas issued under this subtitle for the grounds set forth in this regulation.
Suspension Only. A license may be suspended by the State Superintendent of Schools under the following conditions:

Breach of Contract. A license may be suspended for not more than 365 days if the license holder leaves the employment of a local school system in the absence of an emergency and without the consent of the local board of education in violation of the provisions of the Regular State Teacher’s Contract set forth in COMAR 13A.07.02.01B. If an emergency arises, the local board may not unreasonably withhold its consent.
Failure to Pay Child Support.

The State Superintendent of Schools shall suspend a license on notification by the Department of Human Services, Child Support Enforcement Administration, that the license holder’s failure to pay child support meets the criteria for suspension of a license under Family Law Article, §10-119.3, Annotated Code of Maryland.

Before suspending the license, the State Superintendent shall send written notice to the license holder of the proposed suspension and the right to contest the identity of the individual whose license will be suspended.

An individual may appeal the decision to suspend a license based on failure to pay child support in accordance with State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland. At the appeal hearing, the administrative law judge shall limit the issue to whether the Department of Human Services, Child Support Enforcement Administration, has mistaken the identity of the individual whose license was suspended.

The State Superintendent shall immediately reinstate any license suspended for failure to pay child support if notified by the Department of Human Services, Child Support Enforcement Administration, that the license should be reinstated and the individual otherwise qualifies for the license.
Suspension, Revocation, or Denial. The State Superintendent of Schools shall suspend, deny, or revoke a license if the license holder or applicant:
Pleads guilty or nolo contendere with respect to, receives probation before judgment with respect to, or is convicted of, a crime involving:
Contributing to the delinquency of a minor;
Moral turpitude if the offense bears directly on the individual’s fitness for employment in education;
Sexual offense in the third or fourth degree; or
A controlled dangerous substance offense if:
The offense occurred on school property or during a school event; or

The individual has been convicted and the clerk of the court has certified and reported the controlled dangerous substance conviction to the Department consistent with Criminal Law Article, §5–810, Annotated Code of Maryland, based on a finding by the court that a relationship exists between the conviction and the license;
Willfully and knowingly:
Makes a material misrepresentation or concealment as part of any licensure request;
Files a false report or record, or makes any false document, as part of any licensure request;
Presents a false license or misrepresents one’s licensure status to the Department or an employer; or
Commits a violation of the test security and data reporting policy and procedures set forth in COMAR 13A.03.04;
Fraudulently or deceptively obtains a license;
Knowingly fails to report suspected child abuse in violation of Family Law Article, §5-701, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Is dismissed after an allegation of misconduct involving a student in any school system or any minor is substantiated;
Resigns after notice of allegation of misconduct involving a student in any school system or any minor;
Is dismissed after notice of allegation of misconduct involving any grounds for denial, suspension or revocation of a license provided in this regulation is substantiated;
Resigns after notice of allegation of misconduct involving any grounds for denial, suspension or revocation of a license provided in this regulation; or
Has had a license suspended, revoked, denied, or voluntarily surrendered in another state for a cause which would be grounds for suspension or revocation under this regulation.
Revocation or Denial. The State Superintendent of School shall revoke or deny a license if the license holder or applicant:
Pleads guilty or nolo contendere with respect to, receives probation before judgment with respect to, or is convicted of, a crime involving:
Child abuse or neglect as defined in Criminal Law Article, §§3-601—3-603, Annotated Code of Maryland, or a comparable crime in another state;
Possession, distribution, receipt, or production of child pornography;
Sexual solicitation of a minor; or
A crime of violence as defined in Criminal Law Article, §14-101, Annotated Code of Maryland, or a comparable crime in another state;
Is dismissed after an allegation of sexual child abuse is substantiated; or
Resigns after notice of allegations of sexual child abuse.

section.heading: Petition for Disciplinary Action or Denial.

para.text: Except as provided in Regulation .02B(2) of this chapter, the following individuals shall file a petition notifying the State Superintendent of Schools in writing of grounds against a license holder or applicant under Regulation .02 of this chapter:
The local superintendent of schools or a state agency employer if the:
Individual is currently employed or was employed by the local school system or state agency employer when the conduct occurred; or
Conduct is reported to the local school system in a criminal background investigation required under Family Law Article, §§5-550—5-559, Annotated Code of Maryland;
The administrator of a nonpublic school if the:
Individual is currently employed or was employed by the nonpublic school when the conduct occurred; or
Conduct is reported to the nonpublic school in a criminal background investigation required under Family Law Article, §§5-550—5-559, Annotated Code of Maryland; or
The Assistant State Superintendent of Educator Effectiveness, or the superintendent’s designee.
The petition shall include all of the following:
Name and current or last known address, e-mail, and phone number of the individual against whom the petition is being filed;
Type of license or licenses held by the individual against whom the petition is being filed;
Specific grounds as set forth in Regulation .02 of this chapter and any evidence, documentation, or other information supporting the grounds for denial, suspension, or revocation;
Confirmation that the employee has foregone an appeal or exhausted appeal rights if any employment-related discipline was issued; and
A recommendation on the type of disciplinary action that should be issued, including the following considerations:
The parties may agree to a joint recommendation to the State Superintendent of Schools on the resolution of the case;
The joint recommendation is not binding; and
The State Superintendent of Schools may accept or reject the recommendation, as follows:
Where the State Superintendent of Schools rejects the recommendation of the petitioner under §A of this regulation, the State Superintendent shall recommend the appropriate disciplinary action; and
The petitioner under §A of this regulation shall adopt the State Superintendent’s recommendation in all proceedings related to the licensing action.

The State Superintendent of Schools shall deny, suspend, or revoke a license upon receipt of a proper petition by a local superintendent of schools, an administrator of a nonpublic school, or the Assistant Superintendent of Educator Licensure and Program Approval identifying the grounds against the license holder.
Before denying, suspending or revoking a license, the State Superintendent of Schools shall:
Send the applicant or license holder written notice of the petition; and
Advise the applicant or license holder of the right to request a hearing within 30 calendar days of the date of the written notice.

The State Superintendent of Schools shall e-mail and mail one copy of the written notice and the procedures applicable to the denial, suspension, or revocation of a license by certified mail to the current or last known address of the license holder.
The license holder against whom the petition has been filed may request a hearing in writing within 30 calendar days of the date of the written notice specified in §D of this regulation.

If the license holder does not request a hearing in writing on the petition within the 30-day period set forth in §D(2) of this regulation, the State Superintendent of Schools shall deny, suspend or revoke the license.
Voluntary Surrender.

An educator who is under investigation for, or facing a petition identifying, grounds for disciplinary action or denial as listed in Regulations .02C and D of this chapter may voluntarily surrender his or her license.
The State Superintendent of Schools shall treat a license that is voluntarily surrendered as a revocation, and it may not be reinstated except as described in Regulation .09 of this chapter.
Placing an Alert on an Educator’s Record.
The Department may place an alert on a licensure record on the request of a local school system, nonpublic school, state agency, or on its own accord, if an educator:
Has had action taken on a license by another state; or
Is facing the suspension or revocation of a license after being informed of charges by the State Superintendent of Schools.
An alert does not affect the validity of an educator’s license.
The local school system, nonpublic school, or state agency shall immediately inform the Department if grounds no longer exist to suspend, deny, or revoke an educator’s license.
The Department shall immediately remove the alert from an educator’s record if it becomes aware that grounds no longer exist to deny, suspend or revoke an educator’s license.
Action on an Expired License. The Department may take action against an educator’s license even if the license has expired as long as the basis for the action occurred while the license was active.
Denial.

The Department shall deny a license, permanently or for a fixed period of time, to an individual who does not currently hold a license and has committed grounds listed under Regulation .02C of this chapter.
The Department shall deny a license permanently to an individual who does not currently hold a license and has committed grounds listed under Regulation .02D of this chapter.
An individual who has been denied a license may appeal the decision through the process outlined in Regulations .03—.07 of this chapter.
An individual under investigation for grounds under Regulation .02 of this chapter shall remain ineligible for a license pending the result of the investigation.
Denial Because of a Failure to Pay Child Support.

An individual whose failure to pay child support meets the criteria for denial of a professional license under Family Law Article, §10-119.3, Annotated Code of Maryland, following written notification to the State Superintendent of Schools by the Department of Human Services, Child Support Enforcement Administration, is ineligible for a license.

Before denial of a license, the State Superintendent shall send written notice to the individual, including the right to contest the identity of the individual whose license the Superintendent seeks to deny.

An individual may appeal the decision to deny a license based on failure to pay child support in accordance with State Government Article, Title 10, Subtitle 2, Annotated Code of Maryland. At the appeal hearing, the issue is limited to whether the Department of Human Services, Child Support Enforcement Administration, has mistaken the identity of the individual whose license was denied.

The State Superintendent shall immediately withdraw the denial of an application for a license if notified by the Department of Human Services, Child Support Enforcement Administration, that the individual is eligible for a professional license and the individual otherwise qualifies for a license.
Reciprocal Discipline and Denial.

If a licensing authority in another jurisdiction has sanctioned or taken final disciplinary action against a Maryland licensee or applicant based on grounds for disciplinary action set forth in .02C of this chapter, the State Superintendent may nevertheless deny, suspend, or revoke the licensee's or applicant's Maryland license.
The State Superintendent may adopt the other jurisdiction's sanction or impose an independent sanction consistent with this chapter.
If the sanction has been fully satisfied for all grounds set forth in .02C of this chapter, the State Superintendent may decline to take further disciplinary action in Maryland.

para.text: In this subtitle, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined
“Administration” means the Maryland Cannabis Administration established under Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-201, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Advisory Council” means the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council established under Health-General Article, §13–4502, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Agent.
“Agent” means an employee, a volunteer, or any other authorized person who acts for or at the direction of a cannabis licensee or cannabis registrant.
“Agent” includes:
Cannabis licensee agent;
Cannabis registrant agent;
Owners; and
Management companies or individuals who are employees, volunteers, or otherwise authorized by a management company.
Cannabis.

“Cannabis” means the plant cannabis sativa l. and any part of the plant, including all non-synthetically derived, extracts, cannabinoids, isomers, acids, salts, and salts of isomers, whether growing or not, with a delta–9–tetrahydrocannabinol concentration greater than 0.3 percent on a dry weight basis.
“Cannabis” includes cannabis products, seeds, seedlings, immature plants, and clones.
“Cannabis” does not include hemp or hemp products, as defined in Agriculture Article, §14–101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Cannabis Product.
“Cannabis product” means a product that is composed of cannabis, cannabis concentrate, cannabis extract, or any other ingredient and is intended for use or consumption.
“Cannabis product” includes any product produced and regulated under this subtitle, including:
Cannabis vaporizing devices;
Concentrated cannabis products;
Edible cannabis products; and
Usable cannabis products.
Cannabis Vaporizing Device.
“Cannabis vaporizing device” means a device that can be used to deliver aerosolized or vaporized cannabis or cannabis products to an individual inhaling from the device.
“Cannabis vaporizing device” includes:
A vape pen;
Vaping liquid; and
Any component, part, or accessory of such a device regardless of whether it is sold separately, including a concentrated or infused cannabis liquid, for the purposes of heating and producing a vapor.
Canopy.
“Canopy” means the total square footage of space used by a licensee to produce flowering cannabis plants.
“Canopy” includes each layer of flowering cannabis plants grown on any rack or shelving.
“Canopy” does not include square footage used for:
Mother stock;
Propagation;
Immature or nonflowering plants;
Processing;
Drying;
Curing;
Trimming;
Storage;
Offices;
Hallways;
Pathways;
Work areas; or
Other administrative and nonproduction uses.
“Capsules” means a solid preparation containing a single serving of tetrahydrocannabinol or other cannabinoid that:
Is intended to be swallowed whole;
Not formulated to be chewable, dispersible, effervescent, orally disintegrating, used as a suspension, or consumed in a manner other than swallowed whole; and
Does not contain any added natural or artificial flavor or sweetener.
Caregiver.
“Caregiver” means an individual who has agreed to assist with a qualifying patient’s medical use of cannabis.
“Caregiver” means, for a qualifying patient younger than 18 years old:
A parent or legal guardian; and
Not more than two additional adults designated by the parent or legal guardian.

“Caregiver” does not include any designated school personnel authorized to administer medical cannabis to a student in accordance with the guidelines established under Education Article, §7-446, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Certifying provider” has the meaning stated in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Clinical director” means an individual who:
Is appointed by a licensed dispensary to provide information on medical cannabis to qualifying patients, registered caregivers, and dispensary agents;
Meets the requirements of COMAR 14.17.04.08; and
Is registered with the Administration.
Concentrated Cannabis Product.
“Concentrated cannabis product” means a product derived from cannabis that has undergone a process to concentrate one or more active cannabinoids.
“Concentrated cannabis product” includes:
Kief;
Hashish;
Bubble hash;
Oil;
Wax;
Shatter;
Resin; or
Any other product produced by extracting cannabinoids from the plant using solvents, carbon dioxide, heat, screens, presses or steam distillation.
“Concentrated cannabis product” does not include any cannabis vaporizing device as defined in this regulation.
“Conditional license” means a temporary preapproval for a cannabis license issued pending satisfactory completion of the requirements for licensing under COMAR 14.17.05.
“Consumer” means an individual 21 years old or older who purchases cannabis or a cannabis product from a licensed dispensary or on-site consumption establishment.
Control.
“Control” means:
The decision–making authority over the management, operations, or policies that either guide a business or guide authority over the operation of the technical aspects of a business; or
Authority over the operation of the technical aspects of the business.
“Control” includes:
Holding a right to veto significant events;
The right or authority to make or veto decisions regarding operations and strategic planning, capital allocations, acquisitions, and divestments;
The right or authority to appoint or remove directors, corporate-level officers, or their equivalent;
The right or authority to make major marketing, production, and financial decisions; and
The right or authority to execute exclusive contracts or significant contracts in the aggregate of $10,000 or greater on behalf of the licensee.
“Criminal history record check” means a State and national criminal history records check in accordance with Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-505, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Data network” means the interface with the seed-to-sale tracking system that enables licensees to identify qualifying patients and registered caregivers and monitor patient allotments.
“Delivery service” means a licensee authorized to deliver cannabis in accordance with a micro license to operate a dispensary.
Dispensary.

“Dispensary” means an entity licensed under Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401, Annotated Code of Maryland, that acquires, possesses, repackages, transports, sells, distributes, or dispenses cannabis or cannabis products, including tinctures, aerosols, oils, and ointments, related supplies, and educational materials for use by qualifying patients, caregivers, or consumers through a storefront or through a delivery service, based on license type.
“Dispensary” includes standard and micro license types.
“Disproportionately impacted area” means a geographic area identified by the Office of Social Equity that has had above 150 percent of the State’s 10-year average for cannabis possession charges.
Edible Cannabis Product.
“Edible cannabis product” means a cannabis product intended for human consumption by oral ingestion, in whole or in part.
“Edible cannabis product” includes a cannabis product that dissolves or disintegrates in the mouth.
“Edible cannabis product” does not include any concentrated cannabis products, infused non-edible cannabis products, or capsules or tinctures that do not contain any food or food ingredients.

“Electronic manifest” means the comprehensive report created by a licensee within the Administration’s designated seed-to-sale tracking system to record the chain of custody of a cannabis transfer or delivery.
“Green waste” means unauthorized, misbranded, contaminated, unused, surplus, returned, or out-of-date cannabis or product containing cannabis.
Grower.

“Grower” means an entity licensed under Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401, Annotated Code of Maryland, that cultivates or packages cannabis and is authorized by the Administration to provide cannabis to other licensees and registered independent testing laboratories.
“Grower” includes standard and micro license types.
High Potency Product.

“High potency product” means a product that exceeds the maximum potency for consumers, as established by the Administration, and may only be sold or distributed to a qualifying patient or registered caregiver.
“High potency product” includes:
A concentrated cannabis product that exceeds 1 gram in total weight; and
An edible cannabis product, capsule, or tincture that exceeds 10 milligrams THC per serving and 100 milligrams THC per package.
Home Cultivation Product.
“Home cultivation product” means the clones, seeds, seedlings, stalks, roots, and stems of the cannabis plant for home cultivation.
“Home cultivation product” does not include any plant that is:
Wider than 8 inches;
Taller than 8 inches; or
Otherwise in a vegetative or flowering state.
“Incubator space” means a facility where a micro licensee may operate in accordance with Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-406, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Independent testing laboratory” means a facility, entity, or site that is:
Registered with the Administration to perform tests on cannabis or cannabis products;
Independent of any entity licensed under Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401, Annotated Code of Maryland, to grow, process or dispense cannabis; and
Accredited as operating to International Organization for Standardization (ISO) standard 17025 by an accreditation body:
Operating in accordance with ISO standard ISO/IEC 17011; and
That is a signatory to the International Laboratory Accreditation Cooperation (ILAC) Mutual Recognition Arrangement (MRA).

“Infused non-edible cannabis product” means ointment, salve, suppository, dermal patch, cartridge, or any other product containing cannabis that has been processed so that the dried leaves and flowers are integrated into other material that is not intended for human consumption by inhalation or oral ingestion.

“Law enforcement agency” means a governmental police force, sheriff’s office, security force, or law enforcement organization of the State, a county, or a municipal corporation that by statute, ordinance, or common law is authorized to enforce the general criminal laws of the State.
Licensee.
“Licensee” means a business licensed by the Administration in accordance with Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Licensee” includes any:
Micro grower;
Micro processor;
Micro dispensary;
Standard grower;
Standard processor;
Standard dispensary;
Incubator space; and
On-site consumption establishment.
Liquid Edible Product.
“Liquid edible product” means an edible cannabis product that is a liquid beverage or liquid food-based product for which the intended use is oral consumption.
“Liquid edible product” excludes a tincture as defined in this section.
“Medical and therapeutic claim” means any representation that indicates cannabis will improve, relieve, treat, diagnose, or prevent health conditions or any other ailment.
“Micro license” means a license to operate a cannabis business that does not exceed the limits established in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401(c)(2), Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Neutral age screen” means a mechanism to verify a user's age by requiring them to enter their date of birth to gain access to areas of a website that are not designed for children.
“On-site consumption establishment” means an entity licensed by the Administration to distribute cannabis or cannabis products for on-site consumption other than by smoking indoors.
“Operational” means physically and actively engaged in the cultivation, processing, or dispensing of cannabis.
“Owner” means a person with an ownership interest in a cannabis license.
“Ownership interest” means a direct or indirect equity interest in a cannabis license, including in its shares or stock.
“Passive investor” means an individual or an entity that:
Holds an aggregate ownership interest of less than 5 percent in a cannabis licensee; and
Does not have control of the cannabis licensee.
“Personal use amount” means an amount of:
Cannabis that does not exceed 1.5 ounces;
Concentrated cannabis that does not exceed 12 grams; or
Cannabis products containing no more than 750 milligrams of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol.

“Principal officer” means a board member, a president, a vice president, a secretary, a treasurer, a partner, an officer, a managing member, or any other individual with a profit sharing, financial interest, or revenue sharing arrangement, including an individual with the authority to control a cannabis license.
“Processing” means the manufacture of usable cannabis into a cannabis concentrate or manufacture of a cannabis-infused product.
Processor.
“Processor” means an entity licensed by the Administration in accordance with Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401, Annotated Code of Maryland, that:
Transforms cannabis into another product, or an extract, and packages and labels the cannabis product; and
Is authorized by the Administration to provide cannabis to cannabis licensees and registered independent testing laboratories.
“Processor” includes standard and micro license types.
“Qualifying patient” means an individual who:
Has been provided with a valid written certification by an Administration-registered certifying provider in accordance with a bona fide provider–patient relationship; and
If younger than 18 years old, has a caregiver.
Registrant.
“Registrant” means a business registered by the Administration to operate in the cannabis industry.
“Registrant” includes:
Independent testing laboratory;
Transporter business;
Security guard company; and
Waste disposal company.
Residence.
“Residence” means a house, condominium, apartment, or any other dwelling unit under legal possession of an individual.
“Residence” does not mean a dormitory or other on-campus college or university housing.

“Seed-to-sale tracking system” means a software system procured by the Administration that tracks cannabis from either the seed or immature plant stage, until the cannabis is sold to a patient, caregiver, or consumer.

“Serious adverse event” means an undesirable experience associated with the use of cannabis where the outcome was death, life-threatening, hospitalization, disability or permanent damage, congenital anomaly or birth defect or any other important medical event.
“Social equity applicant” means an applicant for a cannabis license or cannabis registration that:
Has at least 65 percent ownership and control held by one or more individuals who:
Have lived in a disproportionately impacted area for at least 5 of the 10 years immediately preceding the submission of the application;
Attended a public school in a disproportionately impacted area for at least 5 years; or

For at least 2 years, attended a 4-year institution of higher education in the State where at least 40 percent of the individuals who attend the institution of higher education are eligible for a Pell Grant; or
Meets any other criteria established by the Administration.
Social Equity Licensee.
“Social equity licensee” means a social equity applicant who has been awarded a cannabis license.
“Social equity licensee” includes a grower, processor, or dispensary that:
Held a Stage One Preapproval for a license before October 1, 2022; and
Was not operational before October 1, 2022.
“Social Equity Partnership Grant” means a program within the Office of Social Equity that awards grants to promote qualifying partnerships between operational licensees and social equity licensees.
“Standard license” means a license to operate a cannabis business that complies with the limits established in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-401(c)(1), Annotated Code of Maryland.
“State Cannabis Testing Laboratory” means the laboratory operated by the Administration in accordance with Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-204, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Sublingual pouch” means a permeable sachet containing concentrated cannabis product that is intended to be dissolved in the mouth and absorbed buccally or sublingually.
“Tetrahydrocannabinol” or “THC”, unless otherwise specified, means any:
Tetrahydrocannabinol, including delta-8-tetrahydrocannabinol, delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol, and delta-10-tetrahydrocannabinol, regardless of how derived;
Other cannabinoid, other than cannabidiol that the Administration determines to cause intoxication; and
Other chemically similar compound, substance, derivative, or isomer of tetrahydrocannabinol, as identified by the Administration.
“Tincture” means a solution that is:
Dissolved in alcohol, glycerin, or vegetable oil; and
Distributed in a dropper bottle of 4 ounces or less.
Usable Cannabis.
“Usable cannabis” means the dried leaves and flowers of the cannabis plant.

“Usable cannabis” does not include seedlings, seeds, stems, stalks, or roots of the plant or the weight of any noncannabis ingredients combined with cannabis, such as ingredients added to prepare a topical administration.
Usable Cannabis Product.
“Usable cannabis product” means a prepackaged product containing usable cannabis.
“Usable cannabis product” includes:
A pre-rolled amount of usable cannabis;
Securely stored, sealed, and labeled amount of usable cannabis; and
Any other type or amount of usable cannabis that has been wrapped, rolled, or otherwise encased for the purposes of smoking.
Visitor.
“Visitor” means a guest at a licensed or registered premises who is not a registered agent employed by the licensee or registrant.
“Visitor” does not include:

A qualifying patient, registered caregiver, adult-use consumer, or any children who accompany a qualifying patient or registered caregiver for the sole purpose of purchasing cannabis or cannabis products; or
An Administration investigator.
“Written certification” means a certification that:
Is issued by a certifying provider to a qualifying patient with whom the provider has a bona fide provider–patient relationship;

Includes a written statement certifying that, in the certifying provider’s professional opinion, after having completed an assessment of the patient’s medical history and current medical condition, the patient has a condition:
That meets the inclusion criteria and does not meet the exclusion criteria of the certifying provider’s application; and
For which the potential benefits of the medical use of cannabis would likely outweigh the health risks for the patient; and

May include a written statement certifying that, in the certifying provider’s professional opinion, a 30–day supply of medical cannabis would be inadequate to meet the medical needs of the qualifying patient.

section.heading: Issuance of a License or Rescission of a Conditional License.

para.text: In this regulation, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined:
“Good faith effort” means:
For an initial extension, demonstrating active interest in or legal control of or possession of a premises; and
For a second extension, demonstrating legal control of or possession of a premises.
“Premises” means a site that is suitable for cannabis license operations and complies with local planning and zoning requirements.
Conditional License Period.
The conditional license period:
Begins on the day that a conditional license is issued to the selected applicant; and
Expires 24 months after the day that conditional license was issued or at the end of an extension granted by the Administration.
A conditional licensee may apply for an extension of the conditional license.
The Administration may:

Approve up to two requests for extensions of the conditional license period, each not to exceed 6 months, if the Administration determines the conditional licensee has made consistent good faith efforts to establish a cannabis business; and

Use its discretion to determine that a conditional licensee has demonstrated consistent good faith effort if the conditional licensee provides adequate documentation that a political subdivision has unduly burdened its efforts toward becoming operational, as defined in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36-405, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Conditional License Extension Requests:

The conditional licensee shall submit, in a manner determined by the Administration, documentation of active interest in a premise which shall identify the proposed site by address, include explicit use for a cannabis business, and be signed by the conditional licensee and the premises owner:
A letter of intent;
An option to lease or purchase the proposed premises; or
Documentation evidencing permission for use of a premises for cannabis operations.
The conditional licensee shall submit, in a manner determined by the Administration, documentation of control of or possession of a premise:
A clear legal title to the proposed premises;
A fully executed and legally binding lease agreement; or
Other documentation evidencing the conditional licensee has control of or possession of a premise.
During the conditional license period, a conditional licensee shall:
Complete a supplemental license application;
Establish legal control of the proposed site, through lease, purchase, or other means, for the cannabis business;
Notify the Administration of establishment of legal control of the proposed site;
Within 6 months of being issued a conditional license, demonstrate adequate capitalization to enable the business to become operational;
Gain zoning or planning approval from a political subdivision, if applicable; and
Register the business with the State Department of Assessment and Taxation.
During a conditional license period, a conditional licensee may not:
Engage in purchasing, possessing, cultivating, manufacturing, or selling cannabis or cannabis products;
Make any transfer of an ownership interest that causes a change in the individual or entity that holds the controlling ownership interest;
Make any transfer of control, as defined in COMAR 14.17.01; and

If the conditional licensee qualified as a social equity applicant, make any transfer of an ownership interest that causes the conditional licensee to no longer comply with the social equity applicant definition in COMAR 14.17.01.
During a conditional license period, a conditional licensee may obtain additional resources by adding:
Grants and loans from new or existing financial sources not listed in the initial application; and
Owners and passive investors.

Any additional resources obtained by a conditional licensee made under §A(7) of this regulation may not violate this subtitle or Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, Title 36, Subtitle 4, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Rescission of a Conditional License. The Administration may rescind a conditional license if a conditional licensee, or any individual or entity included in the supplemental license application:
Has been convicted of or pleaded nolo contendere to a crime involving moral turpitude, whether or not any appeal or other proceeding is pending to have conviction or plea set aside;
Fraudulently or deceptively attempts to obtain a license;
Is ineligible to hold an ownership interest in or control of a business licensed under Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, Title 36, Subtitle 4, Annotated Code of Maryland;
Fails to reveal any material fact pertaining to the conditional licensee’s qualification for a license;
Fails to submit a complete supplemental license application;
Fails to become licensed and operational within:
24 months after the day the conditional license was issued; or
If granted an extension, the day after the expiration of any extension granted by the Administration;
Fails to comply with §A(5) and (6) of this regulation;
Is not registered or in good standing with the State Department of Assessment and Taxation; or
Has taxes in arrears in any jurisdiction.
The Administration may award a license on a determination that:
The conditional licensee has submitted a complete supplemental license application;
The supplemental license application, including any individual or entity included in the application, does not violate §B of this regulation;
The license fee specified in COMAR 14.17.21 has been paid;
All inspections are passed, and all the conditional licensee’s operations conform to the specifications of the application as approved pursuant to this chapter; and
The proposed premises:
Are under the legal control of the conditional licensee; and
Comply with all zoning and planning requirements.
A licensed business may not grow, process, distribute, dispense, or otherwise begin business operations without approval of written documentation under §C of this regulation by the Administration.
The Administration may not award a license to a business who has registered with the State Department of Assessment and Taxation using a legal name that:
Uses the terms “cannabis”, “marijuana”, or other synonym related to controlled substances;
Suggests the use of cannabis as an intoxicant; or
Incorporates any copyrighted material or trademark or service mark attributable to another entity.
The Administration may suspend, fine, restrict, or revoke a license, including a conditional license, if:
A licensee has fraudulently or deceptively submitted written documentation to the Administration;
A licensee has violated Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, Title 36, Subtitle 11, Annotated Code of Maryland;
A licensee began operations prior to Administration approval; or

It is determined that a licensee has not complied with statements in the application, including statements about standards of operation or employment practices related to diversity, equity, and inclusion.
